user.title: Set up Nimbus
user.description: This creates the Nimbus hub. Before adding loads, use the hub's own "Configure" to set your temperature sensors and tuning defaults once -- then add each load you want forecast (HWS, EV charger, pool, individual circuit breakers -- as many as you like) from the hub's device page, one at a time, without repeating this setup.

device.title: Here is what Nimbus found ({number} of {count}): {name}

question.title: One question about {name}
question.description: Nimbus found more than one source for **{role}** on {name}, or one it wants you to confirm. Pick the one that measures it.

capacity.title: {name}: how much does it hold?
capacity.description: The plan needs your battery's capacity. The Energy Dashboard doesn't record it. Leave it empty to set it later on the Solver tab.

finish.title: Ready to set up

abort.already_configured: Nimbus is already set up -- add loads from its device page instead of adding it again.

menu_options.forecaster: Forecaster settings (shared sensors + tuning for every load/signal)
menu_options.solver_battery: Solver settings (your real battery/grid/solar setup, for dispatch planning)
menu_options.switchboard: Topology diagram settings (grid meter to start -- prices/daily kWh optional, next screen)
menu_options.pricing_suggestions: Review pricing suggestions (nothing changes until you confirm)
menu_options.device_setup: Device setup (what Nimbus found, and who is in charge)

forecaster.title: Nimbus settings (shared by every load/signal)
forecaster.description: Every field on this form is OPTIONAL -- submitting it blank is a complete, working configuration, and Nimbus forecasts fine without any of them. They apply to every load or power signal you add, set once here rather than re-entering them each time: the sensors below give a load's model real system context (was the battery charging at this exact moment?), and the three numbers at the bottom already have sensible defaults.

data.temperature_forecast_sensor: Temperature forecast sensor (optional, used for future predictions)
data.humidity_sensor: Humidity sensor (optional, improves accuracy for weather-sensitive loads)
data.curtailment_sensor: Curtailment switch (optional, for a load run only to soak up otherwise-curtailed solar)
data.battery_sensor: Battery power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.grid_sensor: Grid power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.solar_sensor: Solar power sensor (optional, real measured value -- never an optimizer's own plan/forecast)
data.train_days: Days of history to train on
data.hybrid_recent_days: Hybrid mode: recent days from full-resolution history
data.occupancy_on_means_away: The home / away entity is on while away

data_description.temperature_sensor: A real outdoor/ambient temperature sensor. Used as an input feature so the model can learn e.g. "AC load rises with temperature" -- purely optional, every load forecasts fine without it, just less precisely for weather-sensitive loads.
data_description.temperature_forecast_sensor: Either your weather.* entity directly (e.g. weather.home) -- Nimbus calls weather.get_forecasts (hourly) for you -- or a sensor.* whose own 'forecast' attribute is already a list of datetime/temperature entries. Modern HA weather entities no longer expose 'forecast' as a plain state attribute, so pointing this at a weather.* entity is the simplest option for most installs.
data_description.humidity_sensor: A real outdoor/ambient humidity sensor, same role as temperature above -- helps loads whose behaviour correlates with humidity (e.g. some HVAC/dehumidifier patterns).
data_description.curtailment_sensor: A real, measured signal that's ON while your inverter is actively curtailing solar, such as an export-limit-active state from your inverter or logger. Never another optimiser's control or plan entity. If it also carries a forward-looking 'forecast' attribute (a list of time/value entries), Nimbus reads that too. Not every setup has one, and leaving it blank is fine -- it's only relevant for a load specifically run to absorb otherwise-wasted solar (e.g. a pool heater).
data_description.battery_sensor: Your real, live battery power sensor (positive/negative for charge/discharge, whatever convention your inverter integration uses) -- must be a genuine measurement, not a HAEO/EMHASS/optimizer plan entity, or the model will learn from its own future decisions.
data_description.grid_sensor: Your real, live grid import/export power sensor -- same caution as battery_sensor: a measured value, never an optimizer's own forecast/plan.
data_description.solar_sensor: Your real, live solar production power sensor -- same caution as above.
data_description.forecast_horizon_hours: How many hours ahead each load's forecast array extends. It is never less than the Solver's plan (97 hours), so the Solver has a real forecast for every hour it plans; a longer horizon costs more compute per forecast.
data_description.retrain_hour_local: The local hour (0-23) Nimbus retrains every load's model from scratch against your Recorder history. Pick a quiet hour (e.g. 3am) since a retrain briefly uses real CPU.
data_description.train_days: How many days of Recorder history each retrain looks back over. More days generally means a more stable model, at the cost of a slower retrain and adapting more slowly to a genuine change in your own usage pattern.
data_description.training_source: Recorder history (default) reads full-resolution states but is bounded by your own Recorder purge_keep_days -- fine for most installs, but a low purge setting can leave far less history than train_days requests. Long-term statistics reads hour-bucketed data the Recorder keeps indefinitely, so a 30/90/365-day retrain is always possible, at the cost of hourly-only resolution (blurs a load switching on/off within an hour). Hybrid combines both: recent days at full resolution plus the remainder from long-term statistics, gracefully degrading to whichever source is actually available.
data_description.hybrid_recent_days: Only used when Training data source is set to Hybrid -- how many of the most recent days come from full-resolution Recorder history; the remainder of train_days is filled from long-term statistics instead.
data_description.occupancy_entity: An entity that says whether anyone is home: a person, a zone (home when it counts anyone), a group of people, or a presence binary_sensor or input_boolean. While away, each load's forecast falls to the house's own base load at that time of day, and after a few away days to its own away pattern; away periods are left out of training, so the home forecast is not flattened by them. A load keeps it only where it forecasts better.
data_description.occupancy_on_means_away: Turn on when the entity above is an away switch: on while you are away, off while you are home. Leave off for a presence sensor (on while someone is home). Person and zone entities read the same either way.
data_description.occupancy_departure: When the next trip starts (an input_datetime, a datetime, or a timestamp sensor). From then the forecast is the away one, so it falls when you leave rather than hours later.
data_description.occupancy_return: When you are back. Away until then, home from then, so the forecast climbs before you walk in. Works with or without a departure: set only this while you are already away.

solver_battery.title: Solver: Battery (1 of 3)
solver_battery.description: Which sensor reports your battery's live State of Charge, and the battery's size and power limits. These numbers are also on the Solver tab, where you can change them any time without re-running this wizard. 🔴 = required.

data.solver_battery_soc_sensor: 🔴 Battery State of Charge sensor (%) -- the live sensor your system already reports, e.g. from your inverter's own integration

data_description.solver_battery_soc_sensor: The Solver reads this at the start of every solve to know your real current State of Charge -- must be a genuine measurement (0-100%), not a target/setpoint entity. Everything else about your battery (capacity, power limits, efficiency) is configured separately as live number.* entities so you can tune them without re-running this wizard.
data_description.solver_max_discharge_live_entity: Optional -- leave blank unless your own inverter/logger exposes a real, live number.* entity whose 'max' attribute tracks your hardware's actual current discharge ceiling (not every system has this). When set, the Solver prefers that live value over your plain Max Discharge Power number above, as an extra safety margin against a real hardware limit changing without you updating the number entity. Leaving this blank is the correct choice for almost every install.
data_description.live_solver_battery_capacity_kwh: Usable capacity of the whole system. Blank keeps the current value.
data_description.live_solver_max_charge_kw: The system's AC charge limit, from the inverter. Blank keeps the current value.
data_description.live_solver_max_discharge_kw: The system's AC discharge limit, from the inverter. Blank keeps the current value.

solver_grid.title: Solver: Grid Prices (2 of 3)
solver_grid.description: Your price sources, numbered as the Price sources table shows them. Source 1 is your provider (required). Source 2 is AEMO's regional price, made into your retail price with your site's loss factors (NEM only). Sources 3 and 4 are any other forecasts to compare. Your grid import/export power limits live on their own dashboard number entities. 🔴 = required.

data.solver_import_price_sensor: 🔴 Source 1, buy: your provider's live import price sensor ($/kWh)
data.solver_export_price_sensor: 🔴 Source 1, sell: your provider's live export price sensor ($/kWh)
data.solver_regional_spot_forecast_sensor: Source 2, AEMO: regional price forecast (NEM only, e.g. PD7DAY for your region)
data.solver_regional_spot_current_price_senso: Source 2, AEMO: regional price now (the 5-minute dispatch price; a different sensor from the forecast)
data.solver_loss_factor_tni_sensor: Source 2, AEMO: your site's transmission node (TNI) sensor, for its marginal loss factor
data.solver_loss_factor_dlf_code_sensor: Source 2, AEMO: your site's distribution loss factor (DLF) code sensor
data.solver_import_price_sensor_2: Optional: source 3, buy price forecast (e.g. another retailer's, such as Amber)
data.solver_import_price_sensor_3: Optional: source 4, buy price forecast (e.g. a network tariff's retail estimate)
data.solver_price_event_sensor: Optional: price-event simulation sensor -- a step-point $/kWh delta for testing a price-cap or negative-price event
data.solver_envelope_import_limit_entity: Optional: a live DNSP dynamic import limit (e.g. Open Dynamic Export's opModImpLimW) -- bounds the plan per period on top of your static import limit
data.solver_envelope_export_limit_entity: Optional: a live DNSP dynamic export limit (e.g. Open Dynamic Export's opModExpLimW) -- bounds the plan per period on top of your static export limit
data.site_postcode: Site postcode, for the flex telemetry record's region

data_description.solver_import_price_sensor: Whatever your electricity retailer's own HA integration (Amber, LocalVolts, a generic template sensor, etc.) exposes as the current $/kWh you're charged to import. If this sensor also has its own forecast attribute, the Solver uses it directly for planning; otherwise it holds the current value flat across the whole horizon. Also drives the Topology dashboard card's live price display, as a fallback if the Switchboard wizard's own price field isn't set.
data_description.solver_export_price_sensor: The mirror of the above for what you're paid to export -- same forecast-attribute preference, same Topology dashboard fallback role.
data_description.solver_regional_spot_forecast_sensor: Optional -- a real regional wholesale spot-price forecast (Australian NEM markets only, e.g. a pre-dispatch forecast for your own state's region), used to extend the price plan further into the horizon than your retailer's own forecast reaches. Leave blank to skip this extrapolation -- a clean no-op.
data_description.solver_regional_spot_current_price_senso: Optional -- a real, live/historical wholesale spot-price sensor, used to build a retail-markup-vs-wholesale offset from your own recorded history, and to cross-check the current interval's real retail price against AEMO's own live P5MIN wholesale price (a WARNING logs when they disagree beyond the configured AEMO P5MIN Disagreement Threshold dashboard number). A genuinely different sensor from the forecast one above, not a duplicate field. Leave blank to skip both.
data_description.solver_loss_factor_tni_sensor: Optional -- a sensor whose state is the site's transmission node identifier, for example NCMA. With the DLF code below, Nimbus looks up the site's marginal and distribution loss factors in AEMO's published tables for each financial year, so the AEMO-based price is the regional price times the site's loss factors. LocalVolts v2 2.13.0 and later has this sensor (disabled by default; enable it on the device page). Leave blank to skip.
data_description.solver_loss_factor_dlf_code_sensor: Optional -- a sensor whose state is the site's distribution loss factor code, for example BL0A. Used with the transmission node above; both are needed. LocalVolts v2 has this sensor (disabled by default). Leave blank to skip.
data_description.solver_import_price_sensor_2: Optional -- another buy price forecast to compare and blend with sources 1 and 2, for example another retailer's own forecast. It is scored against the price that settles and counts in the blend only once it has earned a weight; until then it only shows on the Price sources table. Leave blank to skip.
data_description.solver_export_price_sensor_2: The mirror of source 3's buy price, for what you're paid to export.
data_description.solver_import_price_sensor_3: Optional -- a fourth buy price forecast, the same as source 3.
data_description.solver_export_price_sensor_3: The mirror of source 4's buy price, for what you're paid to export.
data_description.solver_price_event_sensor: Optional, and a TEST tool rather than a pricing input. Point this at your own sensor whose `forecast` attribute is a list of step points, each with a time field and a value field, where the value is a $/kWh DELTA -- e.g. +20 from 18:00 to 20:00 to simulate a NEM Market Price Cap event (the real cap is $23.20/kWh), or -1 from 11:00 to 15:00 for a Minimum System Load negative-price floor. The delta is added to BOTH your import and export prices, because a real wholesale price event moves the whole market. End every window with an explicit value of 0 -- a step value holds forward, so a window that is never closed keeps shifting prices on every future solve (Nimbus logs a warning if it sees that). Nothing happens until you also arm switch.nimbus_solver_price_event_enabled, and leaving this blank is a complete no-op.
data_description.solver_envelope_import_limit_entity: Optional. A dynamic connection agent's own live import-limit entity (e.g. Open Dynamic Export's opModImpLimW, published over MQTT once you point HA at it) -- read as a live value, or as a forecast schedule if the entity has one. Leave blank to use only your static import limit above -- a complete no-op.
data_description.solver_envelope_export_limit_entity: The mirror of the above for export (e.g. Open Dynamic Export's opModExpLimW).
data_description.live_solver_grid_max_import_kw: Your connection's import limit. Blank keeps the current value.
data_description.site_postcode: Optional -- your site's 4-digit postcode. The flex telemetry record needs the site's NEM region and the first three digits of its postcode. Nimbus reads them from the Companion App's geocoded location when exactly one phone has it; set this when there is none, or more than one. Leave blank to skip.

advanced.name: Advanced grid settings
advanced.description: Optional. Leave these blank unless you need them: a price-event test sensor, and a live dynamic import or export limit from your network.

solver_sources.title: Solver: Solar & Load Forecasts (3 of 3)
solver_sources.description: Where the Solver gets its forward-looking view of what solar you'll generate and what your house will consume -- point these at your own forecast sensors (Solcast, Open-Meteo, Nimbus's own Power Signals, or anything similar that already exists on your system). Only 2 of the 16 fields here are required -- one solar forecast and one load forecast; the rest are refinements you can add later. Worth knowing: the daily quality report needs all three real-measurement sensors (whole-house, solar power, battery power), so leaving any one blank means Nimbus solves normally but publishes no score at all. 🔴 = required.

data.solver_solar_forecast_sensor: 🔴 Solar generation forecast sensor (kW or kWh) -- your existing solar forecast integration
data.solver_solar_forecast_sensor_2: Optional: second, independently-modeled solar forecast source to blend with the first
data.solver_solar_forecast_sensor_3: Optional: third solar forecast source to blend
data.solver_load_forecast_sensor: 🔴 Household load forecast sensor (kW) -- e.g. a Nimbus Power Signal forecasting your own whole-house load
data.solver_load_forecast_entities: Optional: individual circuit forecast sensors to sum instead of the single sensor above (kW each, e.g. Nimbus Power Signals for specific circuits) -- leave blank to use the sensor above
data.solver_whole_house_cross_check_sensor: Whole-house power sensor (the live one your household load forecast is built from)
data.solver_solar_power_sensor: Optional: real, currently-measured solar power sensor (not a forecast) -- enables the built-in daily EPR/regret quality score. Leave blank to skip scoring.
data.solver_battery_power_sensor: Optional: real, currently-measured net battery power sensor (kW, positive = discharging) -- enables the built-in daily EPR/regret quality score. Leave blank to skip scoring.
data.solver_battery_power_positive_is_charge: Tick ONLY if your battery sensor above reports the opposite convention (positive = charging, negative = discharging) -- e.g. SigEnergy plants. Leave unticked for the far more common positive = discharging convention.
data.solver_p2p_settlement_history_sensor: Optional: a sensor publishing real settled export-bonus history ('{date: {export_cost, export_volume}}') if your retailer has a P2P/VPP program -- improves the quality score's accuracy. Leave blank if you have no such program.
data.solver_price_forecast_array_sensor: Optional: a richer per-5-minute price forecast sensor from your own retailer/market integration, if it publishes one
data.solver_p2p_matched_rate_forecast_sensor: Optional: a sensor publishing real per-interval P2P/community-trading matched-rate data, if your retailer has such a program
data.solver_p2p_matched_rate_forecast_sensor_: Optional, transitional: a second P2P matched-rate sensor, used only for intervals the first does not cover
data.solver_price_comparison_sensors: Optional: price sources to record for comparison only
data.solver_price_spike_alert_entity: Optional: a binary_sensor for a real named price-spike alert product (e.g. Amber's own Spike), if your retailer has one -- the plain $/kWh threshold (Solver settings, live number entity) works without this
data.solver_weather_forecast_sensor: Optional: a weather.* entity (e.g. weather.home, weather.pirateweather) or sensor.* forecast for the dashboard's own Temp/Humidity chart. Leave blank to skip.

data_description.solver_solar_forecast_sensor: Any sensor exposing a forward-looking solar generation forecast (Solcast, Open-Meteo Solar Forecast, or a Nimbus Power Signal pointed at your own inverter's DC power). The Solver reads its forecast attribute directly if present; if the referenced entity has no forecast, its shape is validated and a clear error is surfaced rather than silently producing a flat, useless plan.
data_description.solver_solar_forecast_sensor_2: Optional -- a second, independently-modeled solar forecast (e.g. a different provider from the primary source), blended together the same way multiple import/export price sources are. Leave blank to use only the primary source -- a complete no-op.
data_description.solver_solar_forecast_sensor_3: Optional -- a third solar forecast source, same blending as the second.
data_description.solver_load_forecast_sensor: The single sensor the Solver treats as "total household load" for planning. A Nimbus Power Signal on your own whole-house power meter is the simplest choice -- or leave this and use the per-circuit list below instead, which is summed automatically.
data_description.solver_load_forecast_entities: If you'd rather the Solver build its total household load from several individual circuit forecasts (e.g. one Nimbus load per circuit breaker) instead of one whole-house sensor, list them here -- they're summed together every solve. Leave blank to use the single sensor above instead.
data_description.solver_whole_house_cross_check_sensor: Your live whole-house power sensor, not a forecast. The Forecaster uses it to know which load is the whole house (its overnight spike and stair-step corrections apply to that load only), and the Solver compares its first forecast period against it as a sanity check. It does not change the dispatch plan directly.
data_description.solver_solar_power_sensor: Feeds the built-in quality score (EPR/regret/tracking, sensor.nimbus_solver_quality_report) with what your solar ACTUALLY produced yesterday, to compare the real dispatch against a perfect-foresight oracle. Genuinely different from the forecast sensor above -- this must be a real measurement, not a forecast.
data_description.solver_battery_power_sensor: Same quality-score role as the solar sensor above, for your battery's real net power (positive = discharging, negative = charging) -- both this and the solar sensor are required together for a score to be published.
data_description.solver_battery_power_positive_is_charge: Some hardware (confirmed on SigEnergy) reports the opposite sign to the convention this integration assumes everywhere else. Getting this wrong silently inverts every charge/discharge decision in the quality score, producing a nonsensical result (e.g. a negative EPR) -- if your published score looks impossible, this is the first thing to check.
data_description.solver_p2p_settlement_history_sensor: If your retailer pays a real settlement/bonus rate for exported energy (e.g. a P2P or VPP program), point this at a sensor whose 'history' attribute holds real settled '{date: {export_cost, export_volume}}' entries. Without this, the quality score still works but prices export at your plain configured rate only, missing any real bonus revenue.
data_description.solver_price_forecast_array_sensor: Optional -- any entity whose own 'forecast' attribute is a list of real per-5-minute price points, for a richer near-term price plan than a plain current-price sensor alone. Retailer-agnostic in shape, not tied to any one integration by name. When set, it is the plan's price for every period after the current 5 minutes: it replaces the forecasts of the buy and sell price sources on the Grid Prices step (only the current block is read from source 1's live price). Use your own retailer's forecast here, the same retailer as source 1. Leave blank to fall back to your plain import/export price sensors' own forecast-or-flat behaviour.
data_description.solver_p2p_matched_rate_forecast_sensor: Optional -- any entity whose own 'forecast' attribute lists real per-interval P2P-matching data: either matched cost/volume/proportion rows, or time/value rows giving the matched rate per kWh (with a $/kWh or c/kWh unit and a known interval, e.g. LocalVolts v2's Sell P2P Matched Cost). The empirical rate a community-trading/peer-export program actually paid. A household with no such program leaves this blank forever.
data_description.solver_p2p_matched_rate_forecast_sensor_: Optional and transitional -- not needed to finish setup. A second matched-rate source in either shape above, e.g. LocalVolts v2's Sell P2P Matched Cost alongside its Current Sell Rate. For each interval, the source with the newer data decides, whether it says matched (at any rate, $0 included) or not matched; the other is used only where the first has no answer, and data more than an hour old is ignored. It never changes your P2P blocks or volume. Leave blank to use the first sensor alone.
data_description.solver_price_comparison_sensors: Optional, and never used to plan. Each sensor listed here has its price forecast stored with the Solver's decision records, so different ways of combining price sources can be scored later against what the prices actually were. Amber, AEMO and other retailers' forecast sensors work. Listing one changes no price, plan or dispatch. Leave blank to record only the sources the Solver uses.
data_description.solver_price_spike_alert_entity: Optional -- an ADDITIONAL/alternative trigger for the price-spike discharge override (Solver settings) if your retailer publishes a real named alert product. The plain $/kWh threshold (a live number entity, no wizard field needed) is the primary, fully generic mechanism and works with no retailer integration at all. Either condition triggers detection; the override itself still requires explicitly arming switch.nimbus_solver_price_spike_override_armed.
data_description.solver_weather_forecast_sensor: Optional, purely cosmetic -- feeds the dashboard's own Temp/Humidity chart only, never the actual LP solve. Accepts a weather.* entity directly (Nimbus calls weather.get_forecasts for you) or a sensor.* whose own 'forecast' attribute already carries datetime/temperature[/humidity] entries. Humidity is only published when your chosen source's own forecast actually carries a humidity field.

advanced.name: Advanced sources
advanced.description: Optional extra sources. Leave every one of these blank unless you know you need it — Nimbus works from the two fields above. Add a second or third solar forecast to blend providers, a battery or solar power sensor to score past days, or regional spot and P2P sensors if your retailer publishes them.

switchboard.title: Topology diagram: Switchboard
switchboard.description: Grid power, battery power, and every Load are auto-detected -- nothing to configure here for those. Every field below is optional and covers only what Nimbus has no equivalent for: current prices and the 6 daily-kWh headline stats. Leave anything blank and submit; the diagram works fine without it, add more anytime.

data_description.switchboard_import_price_sensor: Fallback only -- if any Nimbus Solver settings are configured (see "Solver: Grid Prices" above), the Topology card reads price live from there instead and this field is never read. Only fill this in if you're using the Topology diagram without the Solver.
data_description.switchboard_export_price_sensor: Same fallback-only role as the import price field above, for the sell/export price shown on the diagram.
data_description.switchboard_import_energy_daily_sensor: A daily-resetting utility_meter (or equivalent) tracking total kWh imported today -- shown as a headline stat on the Topology diagram. Nimbus has no equivalent of its own for daily energy totals (it forecasts power, not accumulated energy), so this genuinely needs your own sensor.
data_description.switchboard_export_energy_daily_sensor: Same as above, for total kWh exported today.
data_description.switchboard_house_load_energy_daily_sens: Same as above, for total household load energy consumed today.
data_description.switchboard_solar_energy_daily_sensor: Same as above, for total solar energy generated today.
data_description.switchboard_battery_charge_daily_sensor: Same as above, for total energy charged into the battery today.
data_description.switchboard_battery_discharge_daily_sens: Same as above, for total energy discharged from the battery today.

pricing_suggestions.title: Review pricing suggestions
pricing_suggestions.description:
Nimbus found these price sources for Solver price fields that are currently empty:

{suggestions}

**Submit applies exactly these changes**, and each one is logged and listed in a notification. Close this window to leave your pricing as it is.

A field that already has a value is never changed here, even if its sensor is missing right now. To change one, use Solver settings.

device_setup.title: Device setup
device_setup.description: The device setup is in **{mode}** mode.

menu_options.device_setup_dry_run: Dry run: what the device setup would build from your settings
menu_options.device_setup_control: Control: let Nimbus run a controllable load, or stop it

device_setup_dry_run.title: Device setup: dry run

device_setup_mode.title: Device setup: mode
device_setup_mode.description:
Now **{mode}**; the dry run is **{result}**.

- **legacy**: your settings, as always.
- **shadow**: the device setup is kept beside your settings and checked; your settings stay in charge.
- **active**: the device setup is in charge, and your settings are written from it. Needs a clean dry run, and every power sensor's unit known.

device_setup_review.title: Review what Nimbus finds
device_setup_review.description: What Nimbus finds now that differs from your device setup. New sources, renames and new devices are ticked; an alternative to a source you confirmed never is. Untick anything you don't want.

device_setup_nothing.title: Review what Nimbus finds
device_setup_nothing.description: Nothing new: what Nimbus finds matches your device setup.

device_setup_edit.title: Edit a source: which device?
device_setup_edit.description: Choose the device whose source you want to change.

device_setup_edit_source.title: Edit a source: {name}
device_setup_edit_source.description: Choose what to change and the sensor that measures it. Nimbus checks the new sensor (its unit and that it reads) before saving; if it can't be read, nothing changes.

device_setup_control.title: Control: which load?
device_setup_control.description: Nimbus never commands anything unless you allow it here, one load at a time. Finishing setup never allows it.

device_setup_control_device.title: Control: {name}
device_setup_control_device.description: If you tick **Allow**, Nimbus will turn the entity below on and off to run {name} at the times its plan chooses, within the windows, limits and comfort settings you set for it. It is recorded with who allowed it and when. Untick to stop: Nimbus stops commanding it at once.

device_setup_no_control.title: Control
device_setup_no_control.description: There is no controllable load in the device setup. Add one with **+ Add → Controllable Load** on the Nimbus hub.

error.energy_sensor_not_power: This sensor reports an energy unit (Wh or kWh): it is an energy counter, not a power reading. Pick a power sensor (W or kW) instead; most inverters and meters expose both.
error.frozen_price_signal: This price is fixed when the forecast is built and does not follow the live price (LocalVolts Rate All Var). It would hide a price spike from the plan. Pick the live price instead: for LocalVolts, Buy Flex Up or Sell Flex Up.
error.loss_factor_pair_incomplete: AEMO's two loss factor sensors (transmission node and distribution loss factor code) only work together. Set both to turn the regional price into a retail one, or clear both to skip the AEMO source.
error.import_export_same_entity: The same sensor is set as both the buy and sell price for one source. A buy price and a sell price are never the same live sensor -- point this field at your export price sensor instead.
error.mode_refused: That mode change was refused: run the dry run and check every power sensor's unit, then try again.
error.choice_refused: One of the ticked changes is no longer offered. Open the review again.
error.binding_refused: One of the ticked sources can't be read with its unit. Untick it and try again.
error.revision_conflict: The device setup changed while you were reviewing. Open the review again.
error.confirm_refused: The changes could not be saved.
error.unknown_device: That device is no longer in the device setup. Open Edit a source again.
error.choose_shadow_first: Move the device setup to shadow first (Device setup, Dry run).
error.control_entity_needed: Choose the entity Nimbus switches before allowing control.
error.site_postcode_invalid: The site postcode is four digits, for example 4000.

abort.no_pricing_suggestions: There are no pricing suggestions: every price field Nimbus can fill already has a value.
abort.still_starting: Nimbus is still starting and restoring its settings. Try again in a minute.

user.title: {action} a load
user.description: Pick the power sensor this load should learn from. Temperature sensors and tuning settings are shared across every load -- set them once via the hub's own "Configure" instead. The fields below the sensor are optional and genuinely per-load, unlike everything on the hub's shared form -- leave them all blank for a load with no fixed daily schedule and no bursts. 🔴 = required.

data.run_hold_learned_when_off: While off, forecast its usual runs

data_description.load_sensor: A real, measured power sensor for one specific circuit/appliance (kW or W) -- e.g. a smart circuit breaker on your hot water system, pool pump, or EV charger. Nimbus trains a dedicated model against this sensor's own Recorder history and publishes a matching forecast sensor once training completes.
data_description.schedule_start_hour: For a load with a real fixed daily timer (e.g. a pool pump running 8am-3pm every day), the hour it typically starts -- lets the model learn the sharp on/off boundary directly instead of only approximating it through hour-of-day patterns. 24-hour decimal (e.g. 12.5 = 12:30pm), not a 12-hour clock -- avoids any AM/PM ambiguity. Leave blank for a load with no fixed schedule; it's a no-op, not an error.
data_description.schedule_end_hour: The matching end hour for the schedule window above -- same 24-hour decimal format (e.g. 15 = 3pm, 0 = midnight). Only meaningful together with the start hour.
data_description.expected_load_kw: Optional, only meaningful alongside the schedule window above -- roughly how much power this load draws while actually running (e.g. 3.7 for a typical HWS element). Gives the model a sensible starting point for what 'on' looks like, refined further from real history as it retrains.
data_description.running_threshold_kw: For a load that runs in bursts -- a washer, an oven, an AC. While it draws at least this much (e.g. 0.6 for 600 W), the forecast holds its current draw for the hours below, then nothing. While it is below this, nothing is forecast for it. Checked every 2 minutes, so a run that keeps going keeps extending the hold and a switch-off clears it. Leave blank to forecast it from its learned pattern instead.
data_description.run_hold_hours: How long a running load is forecast to keep going from its latest reading (default 1). Only used with the field above.
data_description.run_hold_learned_when_off: Only with 'Running above'. Off: nothing is forecast while the load is off. On: its usual runs, learned from its history, are forecast instead -- for a load with a regular pattern, such as an AC on hot afternoons.

error.duplicate_source_sensor: Another Load or Power Signal already uses this sensor. Pick a different one, or edit the existing entry instead of creating a duplicate.
error.energy_sensor_not_power: This sensor reports an energy unit (Wh or kWh): it is an energy counter, not a power reading. Pick a power sensor (W or kW) instead; most inverters and meters expose both.

user.title: {action} a power signal
user.description: Forecast a real power signal directly -- Battery, Solar, Grid, or anything else -- as its own genuine target, using the same forecasting engine as a load. Pick a real MEASURED sensor, never an optimizer's own plan/forecast entity. 🔴 = required.

data.signal_role: Role (optional -- pick Battery/Solar/Grid so the topology dashboard card can auto-wire this signal; Temperature/Humidity for a weather signal; leave as Other for anything else)

data_description.load_sensor: A real, measured sensor -- e.g. your inverter's total battery power, total DC/solar power, your grid meter's total active power, or (with the Temperature/Humidity role below) a weather sensor. Must be a genuine measurement, not an optimizer's own plan/forecast entity, or the forecaster will learn from its own predictions.
data_description.signal_role: Battery/Solar/Grid are purely a labelling hint for the Topology dashboard card's auto-detection -- no effect on forecasting itself. Temperature/Humidity are different: they tell Nimbus this signal is NOT a power quantity, so the forecast entity gets a real °C/% unit instead of kW, and the coordinator skips a power-unit conversion that would otherwise fail every cycle. Leave as Other for anything else.

error.duplicate_source_sensor: Another Load or Power Signal already uses this sensor. Pick a different one, or edit the existing entry instead of creating a duplicate.
error.energy_sensor_not_power: This sensor reports an energy unit (Wh or kWh): it is an energy counter, not a power reading. Pick a power sensor (W or kW) instead; most inverters and meters expose both.

user.title: {action} a power source (topology diagram)
user.description: One real hardware unit that connects to your switchboard -- an inverter, a hybrid battery/inverter, or a battery-only unit. Pure wiring metadata for the topology dashboard card -- not a forecast target. 🔴 = required.

data.power_source_battery_sensor: Battery power sensor (optional -- leave blank for a PV-only source)

data_description.power_source_name: Free text, purely cosmetic -- whatever label makes sense on your own diagram (e.g. the inverter's model number or a physical location like "Garage Inverter").
data_description.power_source_battery_sensor: This specific inverter's own signed battery power (positive = discharging, negative = charging, matching whatever convention your inverter integration reports). Leave blank if this source has no attached battery (a solar-only inverter).
data_description.power_source_dc_sensor: This specific inverter's own total DC power -- genuinely different from battery power, since it reflects real solar throughput regardless of what the battery is doing. Without it, a fully-charged inverter that's still actively producing solar can look falsely idle on the diagram.

user.title: {action} a PV string (topology diagram)
user.description: One real physical PV string or array. Pure wiring metadata for the topology dashboard card -- not a forecast target. Leave "Power Source" blank if this PV is wired independently (not through any inverter you've added here). 🔴 = required.

data.pv_string_label: Label on the diagram (optional, e.g. "West array")
data.pv_string_power_source: Power Source this string is wired through (optional)

data_description.pv_string_entity: The real, per-string power sensor your inverter reports -- e.g. an MPPT/string-level power register, not the inverter's own total DC power.
data_description.pv_string_label: Free text, purely cosmetic -- e.g. compass direction or roof section ("West array", "Garage roof"). Defaults to a generic label if left blank.
data_description.pv_string_power_source: Which Power Source (inverter) this string physically feeds into, if any. Leave blank for a string wired independently of any inverter you've configured here (e.g. a separate optimizer/micro-inverter setup).

user.title: {action} a battery tower (topology diagram)
user.description: One real physical battery pack/tower. Pure wiring metadata for the topology dashboard card -- not a forecast target. Every field is optional; fill in whichever your hardware actually exposes.

data.battery_tower_power_source: Power Source this tower belongs to (optional)

data_description.battery_tower_soc_sensor: This specific physical tower/pack's own State of Charge (%), if your hardware exposes it per-tower rather than only as one combined battery-wide figure.
data_description.battery_tower_soh_sensor: This tower's own State of Health (%), if your hardware exposes it -- a measure of the pack's remaining capacity relative to new, not related to State of Charge.
data_description.battery_tower_voltage_sensor: This tower's own real-time voltage, if your hardware exposes it per-tower.
data_description.battery_tower_temperature_sensor: This tower's own temperature, if your hardware exposes it per-tower -- shown on the diagram, and can matter for real thermal-derating awareness on some chemistries.
data_description.battery_tower_power_source: Which Power Source (inverter) this tower physically belongs to, if your system has more than one inverter/battery pairing. Leave blank if there's only one Power Source, or if this tower isn't tied to a specific inverter.

user.title: {action} a controllable load
user.description: A load the Solver actually decides the timing or level of -- not just a forecast (see the plain Load subentry for that). Only the fields for your chosen Kind are used; leave the others blank.

data.controllable_load_device_entity: Device to command (optional, e.g. a switch or water_heater)
data.controllable_load_climate_on_hvac_mode: HVAC mode to command when ON (only used if the device above is a climate entity)
data.sheddable_min_fraction: Sheddable: minimum fraction that must always run (0-1, optional)
data.deferrable_value_per_kwh: Deferrable: run as soon as it's this cheap (optional, $/kWh)
data.deferrable_max_kwh_per_day: Deferrable: max energy per day (optional, kWh)
data.deferrable_min_deferral_saving_dollars: Deferrable: don't wait unless it saves at least (optional, $)

data_description.controllable_load_name: A short, real name for this load (e.g. "Pool Pump", "HWS L1") -- becomes this subentry's device title.
data_description.controllable_load_kind: Sheddable: the Solver can reduce it under price pressure, down to an optional minimum fraction. Deferrable: it has a real energy target and deadline (hot water, EV charging) -- the Solver decides WHEN within that window, as a soft-priced preference. Thermal: a real temperature is tracked as a genuine hard guarantee (must reach the target by the deadline), not a priced preference -- for a load whose "must heat every day" promise matters more than any other scheduling consideration.
data_description.controllable_load_device_entity: The real entity this load is physically commanded through -- a switch (turned on/off directly) or a water_heater (commanded via set_operation_mode: "performance" for on, "eco" for off). Leave blank for a load that's only scored/planned, never physically commanded. Also doubles as the default temperature reading (Thermal) and done sensor (Deferrable) for this same load, unless overridden.
data_description.controllable_load_climate_on_hvac_mode: For a climate device entity only: which hvac_mode to request when this load turns ON (e.g. "cool" for an air conditioner). "off" is always used to turn it OFF -- no ambiguity there. Never guessed from the device's own supported modes; a climate device with this left blank logs a warning and stays uncommanded on ON transitions.
data_description.controllable_load_min_hold_minutes: Minimum time between commands to this specific device, overriding the shared default hysteresis. Leave blank to use the shared default.
data_description.controllable_load_max_activations_per_da: Caps how many times this device may be commanded ON per day, regardless of what the Solver would otherwise schedule. Leave blank for no cap.
data_description.controllable_load_reaffirm_after_minutes: If this device is still not doing what Nimbus commanded after this many minutes, Nimbus sends the command again. A re-send never counts against the activations-per-day cap above. Leave blank for 15 minutes; set 0 to never re-send.
data_description.sheddable_nominal_kw: This load's real rated power when running at full draw.
data_description.sheddable_min_fraction: The minimum fraction of nominal power that must always be delivered, even under extreme price pressure. Leave blank for a load that can be shed all the way to zero.
data_description.sheddable_shed_cost: A real $/kWh cost the Solver pays every kWh it sheds -- keeps shedding a genuine last resort rather than the LP's free first choice. Defaults to a high reference value if left blank.
data_description.deferrable_max_power_kw: This load's own real power ceiling while running (e.g. a 3.7kW HWS element).
data_description.deferrable_target_kwh: The real energy amount that must be delivered by the deadline (e.g. enough to reheat a hot water tank).
data_description.deferrable_earliest_hour: The earliest time of day this load may run at all. 0 = midnight. Leave blank for no restriction.
data_description.deferrable_deadline_hour: The real deadline -- cumulative energy delivered must reach the target by this time of day.
data_description.deferrable_shortfall_price: A real $/kWh cost the Solver pays for every kWh short of the target by the deadline. Set high enough (the default) that a genuinely reachable target is always fully met; a genuinely unreachable one costs this instead of breaking the whole plan.
data_description.deferrable_value_per_kwh: Optional -- for a comfort load like hot water: run as soon as the price is at or below this, instead of waiting for the single cheapest hour on paper. The Solver still only ever delivers up to your real target (never more), just prefers to deliver it early and cheaply when it can, rather than defer it into a battery that would fill anyway.
data_description.deferrable_max_kwh_per_day: Optional -- caps how much energy this load may use per real calendar day, independent of the target/deadline above. Mainly useful for a price-gated load with no real target (e.g. a Bitcoin miner running whenever the switchboard's price is low) that would otherwise have nothing else limiting how much it draws.
data_description.deferrable_min_deferral_saving_dollars: Optional -- Nimbus may only push this load past the start of its window if it genuinely expects to save more than this many dollars. Set it per load, so hot water can demand a dollar before it is willing to wait while a pool pump happily chases two cents. Leave blank (or 0) and nothing changes: Nimbus keeps chasing every last cent. Unlike every other preference here, this one is allowed to override a real price signal -- that is the point of it.
data_description.deferrable_done_when: The comparison that means this load is genuinely finished, evaluated against the device entity above's own live state -- e.g. ">= 60" for a tank temperature reaching 60°C. For a water_heater/climate device, this compares its current_temperature attribute and defaults to its own live setpoint (the "temperature" attribute) if left blank; for a binary_sensor device its own "on" state alone is the done condition. Leave blank to always follow the target/deadline as configured above instead.
data_description.thermal_max_power_kw: This load's own real power ceiling while heating (e.g. a heat pump's rated input power).
data_description.thermal_target_temperature_c: The real temperature that must be reached by the deadline -- enforced as a genuine hard constraint, not a priced preference. An unreachable target (a miscalibrated heating rate, an unusually cold start) is relaxed once, automatically, to a soft shortfall price rather than breaking the whole plan -- see the Solver's own log for when this happens.
data_description.thermal_earliest_hour: The start of this load's own earliest-preference window (a small nudge toward heating earlier when two times would otherwise cost the same). 0 = midnight. Heating itself is never blocked outside this window -- only the deadline and any comfort floor below actually constrain it.
data_description.thermal_deadline_hour: The real deadline -- the target temperature must be reached by this time of day.
data_description.thermal_comfort_floor_c: Optional: a mid-day minimum temperature the Solver actively reheats toward if it would otherwise dip below, at the cost below -- not just relying on the device's own passive eco-mode floor defense. Leave blank for no mid-day reheat pressure at all (the temperature is free to drift anywhere down to 0°C between now and the deadline).
data_description.thermal_comfort_floor_cost: The real $/kWh-equivalent cost the Solver pays for every degree-hour spent below the comfort floor above. Only meaningful when the comfort floor is set.
data_description.thermal_heating_rate_c_per_kwh: Optional override (°C gained per kWh delivered) for the value Nimbus's own thermal-rate learner already derives from real recorder history. Leave blank to use the learned value.
data_description.thermal_idle_decay_c_per_hour: Optional override (°C lost per hour while idle) for the value Nimbus's own thermal-rate learner already derives from real recorder history. Leave blank to use the learned value.

user.title: {action} a battery participant
user.description: An ADDITIONAL, independently-metered battery the Solver dispatches on its own (a second inverter, or an EV) -- not your main household battery, which is already configured on the hub's own Solver settings and always stays the "home" participant. Leave every subentry off if you only have the one battery.

data_description.battery_participant_name: A short, real name for this participant (e.g. "Tesla Model Y", "Second Inverter") -- becomes this subentry's device title and identifies it in the Solver's own per-battery output.
data_description.battery_participant_capacity_kwh: This participant's own real usable capacity, independent of the home battery's.
data_description.battery_participant_soc_sensor: This participant's own real State of Charge sensor (%) -- its own, not the home battery's or a combined/averaged figure.
data_description.battery_participant_power_sensor: This participant's own real power sensor (kW). For a shared resource (e.g. two EVs on one DC charger), use whichever sensor actually reflects THIS participant's own flow if one exists, or the shared charger's sensor if that's all your hardware exposes.
data_description.battery_participant_power_positive_is_ch: Whether a positive reading on the power sensor above means this participant is charging. Different hardware/integrations use opposite conventions -- check a real reading while it's actively charging or discharging if unsure.
data_description.battery_participant_max_charge_kw: This participant's own real charge power ceiling.
data_description.battery_participant_max_discharge_kw: This participant's own real discharge power ceiling. Set to 0 for a charge-only participant that never exports back.
data_description.battery_participant_min_soc_percent: The Solver won't plan discharging this participant below this SoC except under real price pressure (a soft preference, not a hard wall) -- e.g. keep an EV drivable.
data_description.battery_participant_max_soc_percent: The Solver won't plan charging this participant above this SoC except under real price pressure. Overridden per-solve by the live charge-limit entity below when one is set.
data_description.battery_participant_efficiency_percent: This participant's own real combined round-trip efficiency (battery chemistry + any inverter/charger conversion loss).
data_description.battery_participant_salvage_value: A real $/kWh credit for energy remaining in THIS participant at the end of a solve's horizon. Leave blank for none (0.0) -- a genuine no-op, same convention as Degradation cost below.
data_description.battery_participant_degradation_cost_per: A real $/kWh cycle-wear cost for THIS participant. Leave blank for none.
data_description.battery_participant_charge_limit_entity: An optional live number entity (e.g. an EV's own charge-limit slider) whose CURRENT value overrides Maximum SoC above for every solve -- so a household changing this in the vehicle's own app doesn't also have to update this wizard.
data_description.battery_participant_available_entity: An optional entity that says whether this participant is here (e.g. "located at home", "charge cable connected"): a binary_sensor, device_tracker, person, sensor, input_boolean or switch. While it is not in one of the states below, this participant cannot charge or discharge at all for the whole solve. Leave blank if this participant is always available (a real second inverter).
data_description.battery_participant_available_states: The states of the availability entity in which this participant can charge or discharge, comma-separated, e.g. "Charging, Connected" for a charger status sensor. Leave blank to use "on" for a binary_sensor, input_boolean or switch, or "home" for a device_tracker or person; a plain sensor needs its states listed here, otherwise it never counts as available. Matching ignores case.
data_description.battery_participant_departure_hour: The wall-clock hour (0-23) this participant needs to be ready by. Leave blank for no deadline. Must be set together with Required SoC by departure below.
data_description.battery_participant_must_have_soc_by_dep: The SoC this participant must reach by Departure hour above -- a real hard requirement, not a preference (e.g. a car needs to be drivable in the morning). Must be set together with Departure hour above.
data_description.battery_participant_shared_charger_group: A short name shared by every participant drawing from the SAME physical charger (e.g. two EVs on one DC charger) -- leave blank if this participant has its own dedicated charger.
data_description.battery_participant_shared_charger_max_k: The shared charger's own real combined power ceiling -- only meaningful when Shared charger group above is set. If more than one participant in the group sets this, the lowest value is used.
data_description.battery_participant_trip_calendar_entity: A calendar whose events describe this vehicle's trips. Put the distance in the event title or description (e.g. "Trip to Brisbane 120 km" or "30 mi") and Nimbus will make sure the pack holds that much energy before the event starts. An event with no distance is ignored. Leave blank to use the fixed Departure hour above instead.
data_description.battery_participant_kwh_per_100km: How much this vehicle uses per 100 km, for turning a trip's distance into kWh. The default suits most passenger EVs; only change it if you know your own figure.
data_description.battery_participant_odometer_entity: Optional. If a trip is already under way, this lets Nimbus require only the charge for the distance still to go. Without it the full trip is required, which errs towards a fuller pack.
data_description.battery_participant_asset_kind: What Nimbus's flex telemetry reports this battery as. Automatic: a vehicle when a Departure hour or a Trip calendar is set, otherwise a stationary battery. Choose Vehicle or Stationary battery to override that.

options.recorder: Recorder history (default, full resolution, bounded by purge_keep_days)

retrain.name: Retrain
retrain.description: Force an immediate retrain of one or more Nimbus load/power-signal coordinators, without waiting for the daily scheduled retrain.

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: One or more Nimbus forecast entities to retrain. Leave blank to retrain every configured Nimbus load and power signal.

solve_now.name: Solve now
solve_now.description: Run one Solver optimisation cycle immediately, instead of waiting for the next scheduled tick. Reuses the exact same solve logic the periodic timer calls -- useful for an automation that watches a real price sensor and wants to react the instant a settled tick actually arrives, rather than guessing at a cron schedule.

compute_quality_report.name: Compute quality report
compute_quality_report.description: Score the Solver's real dispatch against a perfect-foresight oracle for any past window on demand, without waiting for the daily scheduled report. Returns the same EPR/regret/tracking figures published on sensor.nimbus_solver_quality_report, scoped to exactly the window you ask for.

start.name: Start
start.description: Start of the window to score. Must be in the past.

end.name: End
end.description: End of the window to score. Must be strictly after Start and not in the future.

allow_partial.name: Allow partial
allow_partial.description: If the window's history is incomplete, score whatever real data is available rather than refusing to score at all.

rescore_history.name: Rescore history
rescore_history.description: Re-score the last N complete days and write the corrected figures back into the quality report's history table. Use this after a scoring-formula change, when already-scored days are frozen on the old formula and sit next to newer ones with nothing reconciling them. Each day costs a full oracle solve, so this is deliberately explicit and never runs automatically.

days.name: Days
days.description: How many complete days back from today to re-score, starting with yesterday. Each one is a full oracle solve, so start small.

flex_telemetry_record.name: Flex telemetry record
flex_telemetry_record.description: Return the current nem-flex-telemetry schema v2.0 record for the last complete NEM 5-minute interval, built entirely from Nimbus's own entities and last solve. Reads what sensor.nimbus_flex_telemetry already published rather than rebuilding it, so a caller and a dashboard can never disagree about the same interval. Works with switch.nimbus_solver_flex_signals_enabled off: the flexibility fields come from the battery's physical availability, not HiGHS ranging (#1640).

get_stochastic_summary.name: Get stochastic summary
get_stochastic_summary.description: Returns the latest two-stage stochastic dispatch summary (shadow or drive), each scenario's planned battery state of charge and battery power over the horizon, and the solve cadence (last run, last fallback reason, backoff). Read from this install's own Solver, so it is correct even where another install's mirrored plan sensor overwrites this one's. Read-only.

export_decision_inputs.name: Export decision inputs
export_decision_inputs.description: Returns what the Solver decided on in a past window: each solve's first two hours of rows (prices with their source, load, solar, battery, SoC, grid), the full horizon every 30 minutes and whenever the dispatch direction changed, the resolved settings, the price and forecast sources' state at the time, and on each full horizon every price source's own forecast series. Kept 48 hours (heads) and 7 days (full horizons). Read-only; at most 24 hours per call.

end.name: End
end.description: Window end (exclusive). At most 24 hours after start.

kinds.name: Kinds
kinds.description: 'head' (every solve, first two hours) and/or 'horizon' (full plans only). Default: both.

device_contract_preview.name: Preview device setup
device_contract_preview.description: Dry run of moving this install's settings into the device model: the devices it would build, every setting that would change (none, on a clean result), and any conflict to resolve first. Writes nothing.

device_contract_discover.name: Discover device setup
device_contract_discover.description: What Nimbus finds from your Energy Dashboard and recognised price providers: the devices and sources it proposes, the questions it needs answered, and what it read but did not use. With a stored device setup, the differences against it. Changes nothing.

device_contract_confirm.name: Confirm device setup
device_contract_confirm.description: Saves what you accepted from Discover device setup, as a new revision of the stored device setup (shadow or active mode only). Each choice names what discovery offered; anything it did not offer, or a source Nimbus cannot read with its unit and adapter, refuses the whole confirmation and changes nothing.

revision.name: Revision
revision.description: The revision Discover device setup reported. If the device setup changed since, nothing is saved.

choices.name: Choices
choices.description: A list of what you accept: kind, device, role and entity_id as discovery offered them; a new battery also needs capacity (value, unit, basis).

device_contract_set_mode.name: Set device setup mode
device_contract_set_mode.description: legacy (today's settings, the default), shadow (the device model is stored and compared; today's settings stay in charge) or active (the device model is in charge and today's settings are generated from it). Shadow and active are refused unless the dry run is clean, and active only from shadow. Entering active changes no setting; it records the revision your settings now come from.

get_dashboard.name: Get the Nimbus dashboard
get_dashboard.description: Returns this install's Nimbus dashboard (Forecaster, Solver, Topology, Control Panel, Regret and Help tabs) as a dashboard configuration, with the Solver and Help tabs filled in with this install's entities. Copy it into a dashboard's raw configuration editor. Nimbus never creates or changes a dashboard itself. Writes nothing.

device_contract_drift.title: Nimbus: {key} was changed outside the device setup

init.title: Keep {key} or restore it?
init.description:
Nimbus's device setup is in charge (active mode), and it says **{key}** should be **{view}**, but the setting now reads **{current}**. Until you choose, Nimbus keeps running on what the setting says.

**Keep my change** saves {current} into the device setup as a new revision. **Restore** puts {view} back.

abort.not_active: The device setup is no longer in active mode, so there is nothing to choose.
abort.keep_not_possible: This change can't be kept as it is: it disagrees with another setting the same device uses. Change both, or restore.
abort.no_longer_applies: This Nimbus hub no longer exists.
abort.number_not_written: A Nimbus number couldn't be written back. Check the Nimbus number entities are loaded, then try again.
abort.revision_conflict: The device setup changed while you were choosing. Open the Repair again.

device_contract_inconsistent.title: Nimbus: device setup out of step
device_contract_inconsistent.description: The settings say the device setup is at revision {options_revision}, but its saved copy is only at revision {store_revision}. Nimbus can't tell which is right, so it has gone back to shadow mode: your settings are in charge again and nothing has been changed. Check the settings, then run the Nimbus action **Set device setup mode** to go back to active.

forecast_not_trained.title: Nimbus: no forecast yet for {name}
forecast_not_trained.description:
Nimbus has not been able to train a forecast for **{name}**: {reason}.

Usually this needs a few more days of history (about five days of the sensor's own readings). If the sensor has been running longer than that, check in Settings → Devices & services → Nimbus that this Load or Power Signal points at the right power sensor. This message clears itself once a forecast is trained.

frozen_price_input.title: Nimbus: a price setting does not follow the live price

non_power_unit_power_input.title: Nimbus: a power setting points at a sensor that is not in W or kW

energy_unit_power_input.title: Nimbus: an energy total is set where a power sensor is needed

fees_on_top_of_flex_up.title: Nimbus: network fees are counted twice
fees_on_top_of_flex_up.description: Your import price is `{flex_up}` (LocalVolts v2 Buy Flex Up), which already includes your network and flat fees. Nimbus also adds its own fees on top ({fees}), so the plan sees grid energy as dearer than it is and imports less than it should. Set those fee rates to 0 on the Solver dashboard, or in Configure → Solver settings. This message clears itself once they are 0.

fees_on_top_of_pd7day_tariff.title: Nimbus: network fees are counted twice
fees_on_top_of_pd7day_tariff.description: Your import price is `{tariff}`, a NEM PD7DAY tariff sensor, whose price already includes that tariff's network charge. Nimbus also adds its own fees on top ({fees}), so the plan sees grid energy as dearer than it is and imports less than it should. Set those fee rates to 0 on the Solver dashboard, or in Configure → Solver settings, or point the import price at the plain spot forecast instead. This message clears itself once fixed.

regional_forecast_missing.title: Nimbus: no AEMO regional forecast is set
regional_forecast_missing.description: Your prices come from an Australian NEM retailer, but Nimbus has no regional spot forecast. So prices past the end of your retailer's own forecast are held at one flat level, and if your retailer's prices stop updating Nimbus has no AEMO price to fall back to. {found} {where} This message clears itself once the field is set.

solver_input_missing.title: Nimbus: the Solver is missing an input
solver_input_missing.description: The Solver cannot plan properly without: **{inputs}**. Set them in Nimbus → Configure → Solver settings. This message clears itself once they are set.

setup_fill_battery_power.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's battery power?

confirm.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's battery power?
confirm.description:
The Solver's **battery power** sensor is empty. You already chose `{sensor}` as the battery sensor in Forecaster settings, so Nimbus can use the same sensor here.

It reads **{reading}** right now.

{sign}

Submit sets this one field and nothing else. Nothing is sent to any device. To change it later, use Nimbus → Configure → Solver settings; Nimbus will not offer it again.

abort.no_longer_applies: Nothing was changed: that field is already set, or the sensor is no longer a power sensor. This message will update itself.

setup_fill_solar_power.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's solar power?

confirm.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's solar power?
confirm.description:
The Solver's **solar power** sensor is empty. You already chose `{sensor}` as the solar sensor in Forecaster settings, so Nimbus can use the same sensor here.

It reads **{reading}** right now. It must be your **total** solar output, every inverter included. If it covers only one inverter, do not submit: set the total in Nimbus → Configure → Solver settings instead.

Submit sets this one field and nothing else. Nothing is sent to any device, and Nimbus will not offer it again.

abort.no_longer_applies: Nothing was changed: that field is already set, or the sensor is no longer a power sensor. This message will update itself.

setup_fill_cross_check.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's whole-house cross-check?

confirm.title: Nimbus: use {sensor} for the Solver's whole-house cross-check?
confirm.description:
The Solver's **whole-house cross-check** is empty. Your household load forecast is trained on `{sensor}`, so Nimbus can cross-check against the same sensor.

It reads **{reading}** right now.

Submit sets this one field and nothing else. Nothing is sent to any device, and Nimbus will not offer it again.

abort.no_longer_applies: Nothing was changed: that field is already set, or the sensor is no longer a power sensor. This message will update itself.

setup_fill_blocked.title: Nimbus: {field} cannot be filled from {sensor}
setup_fill_blocked.description:
Nimbus could fill the **{field}** from `{sensor}`, which you already chose elsewhere, but {reason}.

Pick a power sensor (W or kW) in Nimbus → Configure, or set the {field} yourself in Solver settings. This message clears itself once that is fixed.

placeholder_settings.title: Nimbus: battery or grid numbers are still placeholders

contradictory_settings.title: Nimbus: battery settings contradict each other
contradictory_settings.description:
{settings}

Fix them on the Nimbus dashboard's **Solver tab → Basic settings → Battery card**. This message clears itself once they agree.

init.title: What unit is {entity_id} in?
init.description:
Nimbus reads **{entity_id}** as a power sensor, and it states {stated}. Today Nimbus takes that as kW. Before the device setup can be in charge (active mode), Nimbus needs to know for sure.

Choose the unit the sensor reports in. You can also fix the sensor's own unit instead; this Repair then clears by itself.

abort.not_in_use: The device setup is in legacy mode, so nothing reads this yet.
abort.no_longer_applies: This sensor is no longer part of the device setup.
abort.revision_conflict: The device setup changed while you were choosing. Open the Repair again.
abort.number_not_written: A Nimbus number couldn't be written back. Check the Nimbus number entities are loaded, then try again.
abort.document_invalid: That unit couldn't be saved into the device setup.

whole_house_sensor_unset.title: Nimbus: no whole-house sensor is set
whole_house_sensor_unset.description: You have a load forecast, but Nimbus does not know which of your sensors is the whole house. Without it, no load gets the Forecaster's whole-house fixes (the overnight spike and stair-step corrections). Set **the whole-house sensor** in Nimbus → Configure → Solver: Solar & Load Forecasts (3 of 3): the live whole-house power sensor your household load forecast is built from. This message clears itself once it is set.

plan_failing_error.title: Nimbus: no new plan for {cycles} cycles
plan_failing_error.description:
Since {since}, the solver has stopped before finding a plan on each of the last {cycles} cycles (the solver's reason: {reason}). Nimbus is keeping its last good plan; once that is five minutes old, the battery forecast shows as unavailable rather than as a plan it never made.

This happens when a solve runs out of time or the solver reports an internal error. The Nimbus log has one line per failed cycle with the solver's details. This clears itself on the next good plan.

plan_failing_infeasible.title: Nimbus: no plan meets your settings

availability_states_never_match.title: Nimbus: {name} is never available
availability_states_never_match.description:
{name}'s availability entity `{entity}` reported only these states in the last {days} days: **{seen}**. None of them is in its "States that mean available" (**{listed}**), so Nimbus reads {name} as away on every cycle and never plans it, even while it is plugged in.

If one of those states means available, add it in Nimbus → {name} → the cog → **States that mean available** (matched ignoring case). If {name} really has been away all that time, nothing needs changing. This message clears itself once a reported state matches the list.

new_install_setup_failed.title: Nimbus could not save the site you confirmed
new_install_setup_failed.description: Nimbus started without the site you confirmed during setup ({reason}). Nothing was changed. Open Configure on the Nimbus hub to set it up there.
